The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Trail That Took a Nap

Daisy walked the path to the birdhouse in twelve quick hops. “A lovely short walk for Everybody Day,” she said. Behind her came Toad. He had done one hop. It had been a very good hop.

“I saved you the easy route,” Daisy told him. “Lovely,” he said. “Did you save me anywhere to stop?” Daisy looked back. She had measured the path in hops. She hadn’t measured it in sits.

She dragged a stool out to the middle. Toad climbed onto it. The sun warmed his back. It warmed his toes. It warmed the stool. “I shall shortly be toast,” he said.

“Where would you put a sit?” Daisy asked. Toad took her along the hedge. He knew a stone beneath a dock leaf. It was cool. It was flat. It fitted a toad exceedingly well.

Daisy sat too. From down there she saw a second shady stone. Beyond that was a patch of clover. The walk along the hedge was longer. The distance from one good sit to the next was shorter.

They tried it together. Walk a bit, sit a bit. Toad told her which stone stayed cool after lunch. Daisy told him which clover patch smelled like honey. Somewhere between sits, they became rather good company.

At the gate Daisy drew a broad leaf over a flat stone on a scrap of paper. She set the picture beside the hedge path for visitors coming through the gate. She made a twin drawing for the Welcome Tree.

“How long does the new way take?” asked Chip. Daisy thought about the shade and the honey smell and a joke Toad had told at the second sit. “Oh,” she said, “about one very nice visit.”

Read together

How would you plan a trip if one friend likes to stop often?
